test: Test 8 (diagnostic): why do on-board clusters (Acc ~77.4%) fall short of oracle clusters (81.0%)?
method: As tests 5 and 7 (MNO on saved B0 maps + release temporal filter, 3 repeats, cluster nodes sigma_G 0.30, epsilon_G 0.50, Arun weight x0.25). References from test 5: B0, B0+KO, B0+KB.

configs.B0+KOC: oracle grouping (GT group of each map object) but only map objects that pass the on-board candidate filter (w <= 0.5, 0.08 <= h <= 0.6, |z - z_robot| <= 0.35); >= 2 members
configs.B0+KBT: on-board clusters exactly as B0+KB (single linkage 0.7 m, 2..10 members, radius <= 1.0 m) with false clusters (no GT group holding >= 50% of members) removed by GT

reading.KO vs KOC: effect of member selection (candidate filter) with perfect grouping
reading.KB vs KBT: effect of false clusters with on-board grouping
reading.KOC vs KBT: effect of on-board clustering itself (splits, merges, extra non-box members)

decision: diagnostic only; no improvement claim. The largest of the three differences in mean Acc names the main cause of the gap.
